newsitem.title: USA: Tietmeyer sees no scope for German rate change.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer sees no scope for German rate change.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Sunday that he saw no need for a change in German interest rates.

Speaking to reporters after a news conference following a G7 finance ministers and central bank governors meeting, Tietmeyer said, "I don't see any room for a change in interest rates, either a reduction or an increase."

The Bundesbank president said that in his view foreign exchange rates roughly reflect economic fundamentals. "All in all, I have the impression that rates are appropriate and reflect fundamental," Tietmeyer said.
Tietmeyer also repeated that Germany favors a strong mark.
He said that he "can't go along with" forecasts that the mark could fall to a yearly average of 1.80 to the dollar.

Tietmeyer said that International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus told a meeting of the Group of Seven finance officials that monetary policy in Europe is currently appropriate and that it cannot make a contribution to solving the continent's unemployment problems.
The German central banker said current conditions in financial markets are "more sound" than they have been in the past.
